revenue_segments.name: Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking
revenue_segments.revenue: 3,771 USD millions net revenue (Q2 2026); net income 1,530
revenue_segments.commentary: Largest earnings driver. Growth came from higher loan and deposit balances, higher capital markets revenue (including BTIG from June 1, 2026) and trust and investment management fees. Noninterest expense rose 8.5%, and provision fell 27.5% on improving credit quality.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, MD&A Business Segment Financial Review; Table 11

revenue_segments.name: Consumer and Business Banking
revenue_segments.revenue: 2,373 USD millions net revenue (Q2 2026); net income 589
revenue_segments.commentary: Revenue was flat. Net interest income slipped 0.3% and expense fell 0.5%. Provision more than doubled from 37 to 78 on higher net charge-offs and the impact of prior-year loan sales. Average loans fell 3.7%.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, MD&A Business Segment Financial Review; Table 11

revenue_segments.name: Payment Services
revenue_segments.revenue: 1,812 USD millions net revenue (Q2 2026); net income 225
revenue_segments.commentary: Net interest income rose 6.0% on higher average loans, and noninterest income rose 5.5% on card, corporate payment and merchant processing. Noninterest expense jumped 10.9% on compensation and marketing, which compressed net income.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, MD&A Business Segment Financial Review; Table 11

revenue_segments.commentary: Improvement reflected better earning asset mix, lower funding costs and fixed asset repricing, partly offset by lower cash balances. Noninterest expense rose 10.5%.

forward_guidance.text: The 10-Q contains no explicit numerical guidance for Q3 2026 or full-year 2026. Forward-looking items in the filing: (1) management describes a relatively neutral net interest income profile to a parallel 50 bp rate shift; (2) BTIG trading activities are expected to enter the Market Risk Rule regulatory capital calculations beginning in Q3 2026; (3) management expects the March 2026 federal capital-rule proposals to be favorable, but exact impacts are unknown until they are finalized; (4) $1.4 billion of parent company debt matures in the remainder of 2026; (5) up to $275 million of additional BTIG cash consideration is payable over three years, subject to performance targets; (6) the Visa interchange injunctive settlement final approval hearing is set for November 16, 2026.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, MD&A Interest Rate Risk Management; Market Risk Management; Capital Management; Liquidity Risk Management; Note 3; Note 15

key_risks.description: BTIG acquisition integration risk. Closed June 1, 2026 for about $395M cash, 6.6M shares and up to $275M of contingent cash. Benefits may take longer than anticipated, or may not be achieved, and costs may exceed expectations. Preliminary goodwill is $613M and subject to adjustment for a year. BTIG also adds trading market risk that will enter regulatory capital calculations from Q3 2026.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, Safe Harbor Statement; Note 3 Business Combinations; Market Risk Management

key_risks.description: Credit card losses and delinquencies. Q2 credit card net charge-off rate was 3.83% on $38.4B average balances, and 30-89 day delinquencies were 1.17% of balances. Consumer credit could deteriorate with higher unemployment; the allowance baseline assumes unemployment of about 4.5-4.6%.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, Table 7; Delinquent loan tables; Analysis and Determination of the Allowance for Credit Losses

key_risks.description: Commercial real estate and commercial criticized loans. Total criticized loans were $7.8B (CRE $3.4B, commercial $3.3B). CRE nonperforming loans were $568M, up from $518M at year-end, and CRE 90+ days past due plus nonperforming was 1.09% of loans. Management lists changes in commercial real estate occupancy rates as a risk.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, Note 5 credit quality table; Table 5; Table 6; Safe Harbor Statement

key_risks.description: Reliance on wholesale funding. Short-term borrowings rose $20.2B to $37.3B in 2026, mainly short-term FHLB balances, while deposits grew only $9.9B. Time deposits are shrinking and average savings balances are growing.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, MD&A Balance Sheet Analysis - Borrowings; Liquidity Risk Management

key_risks.description: Interest rate and securities valuation exposure. Net unrealized losses on AFS securities were $4.4B, and HTM securities carry $9.5B of unrealized losses (fair value 64.6B vs amortized cost 74.1B). Accumulated other comprehensive loss was $7.1B. The company reports no plans to sell AFS securities with unrealized losses.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, Note 4 Investment Securities; Consolidated Balance Sheet; Note 9

key_risks.description: Regulatory and fair-access scrutiny. The OCC and other agencies are conducting inquiries or investigations into fair access to banking, including under Executive Order 14331, which could lead to fines, restitution or business practice changes. The company also faces ongoing RMBS trustee litigation and Visa litigation exposure through swap liabilities (fair value $74M).
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, Note 15 Guarantees and Contingent Liabilities - Regulatory Matters; Visa Litigation; Note 12

key_risks.description: Macro and policy risk. Management cites trade policy and tariffs, geopolitical events including the conflict in the Middle East, inflation, slower growth or recession, and rising unemployment as factors that could hurt results.

GNMA-related delinquent loans and foreclosure exposure. Purchased or purchasable GNMA loans 90+ days past due rose to $3.9B from $3.5B. Residential mortgages in foreclosure rose to $902M from $705M, though repayments are insured by the FHA or guaranteed by the VA.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q filed 2026-08-06, Table 5 footnote; Note 5 Loans and Allowance for Credit Losses

bull_case: Operating leverage is improving. Q2 total net revenue grew 10.1% against 5.9% expense growth, the efficiency ratio improved to 57.1% from 59.2%, and diluted EPS rose 21.6% to $1.35.
Net interest margin is expanding (2.79% vs 2.66%) on loan growth, better earning asset mix and fixed-asset repricing. Average loans rose 7.1% while interest-bearing deposit costs fell.

Fee revenue is broad-based, up 13.2% (capital markets +62.5%, trust and investment management +11.7%, lending and deposit fees +11.2%), and BTIG adds institutional trading and investment banking capability from June 1.

Credit is stable to improving. Net charge-offs fell to 0.53% of loans, nonperforming assets dropped 15.3% to $1.35B, the allowance covers 612% of nonperforming loans, and commercial segment reserves fell on improved credit quality.

Capital and returns are solid. CET1 is 10.8%, return on tangible common equity is 18.7%, tangible book value per share is up 13.3% YoY to $30.04, and the dividend was raised 4% to $0.52. Management expects the proposed capital rule changes to be favorable.
Total available liquidity is $301.7B and the LCR is 107.6%, and the Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking segment is delivering 30% net income growth.
bear_case: Net interest margin of 2.79% is still low in absolute terms, and consumer and payments segments are not contributing growth. Consumer and Business Banking net income fell 4.4% and Payment Services net income fell 4.3% in Q2.
Noninterest expense is rising on technology, marketing (+34.2%) and compensation, and BTIG will add to the expense base. Payment Services expense grew 10.9% in the quarter.

Credit card net charge-offs remain high at 3.83% and loans modified for borrowers in financial difficulty totaled $1.1B in Q2. Criticized loans are still $7.8B, CRE nonperforming loans increased and charge-offs in commercial loans rose.
Wholesale funding has grown. Short-term borrowings are up $20.2B in six months, the net interest margin benefits partly from loan growth funded this way, and time deposit balances are falling.
Balance sheet carries large unrealized securities losses ($4.4B AFS, $9.5B HTM) and a $7.1B accumulated other comprehensive loss, which limits flexibility.
The allowance ratio dropped to 1.94% from 2.03%, so credit reserve releases may not be repeatable if conditions worsen. Securities repositioning produced net losses of $84M in the first half.
BTIG integration, contingent payments of up to $275M, and added trading market risk all raise execution risk. Regulatory inquiries and litigation add uncertainty.
The share price, up 33.5% YoY to $60.40 (per Table 1), already reflects much of the improvement.

what_to_watch.text: Q3 2026 results: whether net interest margin keeps expanding from 2.79% and whether Q2's 10.1% revenue growth against 5.9% expense growth (efficiency ratio 57.1%) holds, with BTIG now included for a full quarter.
Credit card net charge-off rate (3.83% in Q2), delinquency trends, and CRE criticized and nonperforming loans, plus whether reserve releases continue, since the allowance ratio is down to 1.94%.

BTIG contribution to capital markets revenue, trading results and expenses; inclusion of BTIG trading in Market Risk Rule capital calculations from Q3 2026; and any goodwill or purchase accounting adjustments.
Funding mix: short-term borrowings ($37.3B), savings deposit growth and time deposit run-off, and the effect on funding costs and the net interest margin.

Capital: finalization of the March 2026 U.S. bank capital proposals and the effect on CET1 (10.8%); pace of buybacks, with $3.9B remaining under the $5.0B authorization; the dividend ($0.52 per quarter).
Visa interchange injunctive settlement final approval hearing on November 16, 2026, and effects on Visa swap liabilities and card economics.
Securities portfolio repositioning losses ($49M in Q2) and any further sales of AFS securities.
